name: librenms
description: Imports three devices and one ARP endpoint from a real LibreNMS that has genuinely polled a real SNMP agent over the network. The ports, the ifPhysAddress, the bound addresses and the ARP entry all come from an actual SNMP walk, and the SNMP credentials the /devices table hands back in cleartext are asserted never to reach a runZero attribute.
_ready_note: In this order because the API answers 500, not 401, until the migrations are in -- so an HTTP gate alone would either pass on a broken instance or need to accept 500 and prove nothing. A 401 from the real API is the first moment the endpoint under test is genuinely serving: it means Laravel booted, the schema exists, and the route resolved as far as authentication.
_kwargs_note: port_columns is deliberately NOT passed. Its default value is a comma-separated column list, and the runZero CLI splits a --kwargs value on commas into a fabricated second parameter -- so passing it would break the run in a way that looks like an integration bug. Letting the default apply is also the stronger test: it proves the column list this integration ships still matches the LibreNMS ports schema. collect_fdb is switched ON, against its default, because an empty forwarding table is a 404 here rather than an empty array, and that is a real response worth walking into.

fields._match.behavior: no-id-match no-id-break mac-match mac-break ip-match ip-break name-match name-break

log_contains: librenms: /resources/fdb returned 404 (Fdb entry does not exist); treating it as empty

_expect_notes.credentials: The strongest assertion here, and the reason this case exists at all. LibreNMS builds /devices from a plain SELECT d.* and the Device model declares no hidden fields, so the response really does carry community for the v2c device and authname/authpass/cryptopass for the v3 one -- verified against 26.6.1, a current release, not inferred from an old advisory. The seed FAILS if those columns ever stop being returned, because at that moment these fields_absent assertions would be proving nothing. What they prove today is that the integration's attribute set is an allowlist rather than a copy of the record.
_expect_notes.agent: 10.221.9.5 is an actual net-snmp agent in this stack, discovered and polled over SNMPv2c. Everything asserted on it came off the wire: sysObjectID .1.3.6.1.4.1.8072.3.2.10 is net-snmp's own agent OID, sysContact and location come from snmpd.conf, and the two ports are the container's real lo and eth0.
_expect_notes.loopback: ipAddresses is asserted as exactly 10.221.9.5, and that is a record-level assertion rather than a decorative one. /devices/{id}/ip really returns TWO rows for this device -- 10.221.9.5/24 on eth0 and 127.0.0.1/8 on lo -- because a Linux agent publishes its loopback over IP-MIB like any other address. The platform would filter 127.0.0.1 on the way out regardless, so only asserting the exact surviving set proves the integration dropped it itself.
_expect_notes.port_macs: ifPhysAddress arrives from LibreNMS as bare 12-character hex, 02420add0905, with no separators -- Mac::hex() is documented that way and the colon form exists only for display. The emitted 00:42:0a:dd:09:05 differs in the second nibble because network_interface() clears the locally-administered bit that Docker's 02:42 prefix sets. lo's ifPhysAddress is NULL and contributes nothing, which is why the device carries one MAC and not two.
_expect_notes.endpoint: Not seeded -- earned. The agent holds an ARP entry for 10.221.9.4 because the LibreNMS poller had just talked to it, so this endpoint asset is the byproduct of one container polling another. _match.behavior is asserted because no-id-match is the only place that decision is observable: the id is a MAC, and a MAC that is reassigned, spoofed, or randomized must never be able to pull a different device onto an existing asset.
_expect_notes.not_asserted: Three fields the real agent returns are deliberately left unasserted because they describe the HOST this test runs on, not the software under test: sysDescr and version carry the host's kernel release, and hardware carries its CPU architecture (Generic ARMv8 64-bit here, something else on an Intel machine). Asserting them would make this case fail on a different laptop for a reason that has nothing to do with LibreNMS. uptime and the last_polled/last_discovered timestamps move between runs for the same reason.
_expect_notes.v3_device: Never polled, so /devices/{id}/ip and /devices/{id}/ports both answer a real 404 and the integration has to treat that as empty rather than as a failure. Its sysName is the bare IP LibreNMS defaults to, which is why it emits an address and no hostname at all.

_invariants_skip_reason.no_mac_in_id: Deliberate design, matching the librenms fixture scenarios. An ARP or FDB row has no identifier but its MAC, so the endpoint id is librenms:<server>:endpoint:<mac>. It is paired with no-id-match no-id-break precisely so that id can never drive a merge, and that pairing is asserted above rather than assumed.
